snippet.textDisplay: 13:47 honestly, we have slowly been giving away our jobs to technology without realizing it. Every single time that we developed technology that made things easier and more efficient, we all were excited at first that it will help us, but a lot of people were replaced as a result. Mail, for example, is now text messages and e-mails. There were 100 people needing to write or type out the letters, now you only need 5-10. The other 90-95 people had to figure something else out. Over time, we have reduced what we need. We all thought "I can get all this done in HALF THE TIME" what ended up happening is people were laid off, you were handed their work, so you single handedly do the work of 100 people with the help of technology, and nobody's work hours got reduced, they went from 6 hour shifts to 8 hour shifts and overtime. Because the goal of the corporation is not for you to enjoy your life and time, it's for them to squeeze the most they can out of you. Just look at our job market. Back in the day, you would get hired straight out of school because you were needed, now, jobs is something we compete for, we have thousands of applicants to 1 job posting. And this is going to just become harder and harder.

snippet.textDisplay:
We could all have 5x as much health care for the same price? 
He's either the dumbest smart person or the smartest dumb person I've ever seen. You could flip the outcomes of the two analogies and just as easily present them both as true. And neither set of analogies is more correct than the other as they both miss the main point, which is an underlying theme in both analogies, so either set of examples was only 50% correct. 

Where the function of a matter involves a transactional exchange of wealth, the person/entity in control and/or in possession of said wealth and the matters surrounding its transfer from external sources to its control and/or possession in almost every circumstance is going to exploit this increase in thier potential margins to realise greater gains. 

No business outside of genuine charities acts to do anything other than maximise their profitability / returns. 

We won't get 5x more healthcare. He said it himself, there's no limit to the healthcare people want. Meaning the market will ALWAYS have more demand then supply and the balance of bargaining power will ALWAYS lay with the goods/service provider in a market such as healthcare. This means that the vast majority of benefits will be enjoyed by that which benefits from any cost reductions or increased volume of turnover. 

We still have unaffordable health care... But healthcare becomes 5x better at generating returns. But it will still cry poor...
